name: Larvik
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging Larvik | Ferry and Short-Sea Ships
description: UTM in Larvik for the Hirtshals ferry, container feeders, general cargo and stone-carrying bulk ships: car-deck, hold, tank-top and scrubber pipe gauging.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ferries and Cargo Ships at the Port of Larvik
intro: Larvik sits at the inner end of the Larviksfjord on Vestfold's southern coast, with a ferry crossing to Hirtshals in Denmark and a cargo port handling containers, general cargo and bulk. Ships here keep regular schedules, so gauging is fitted into turnarounds, cargo stays and planned lay days. Atlantis does not keep anyone in Larvik: for each job a team flies from India to the ship and works to a scope agreed with the superintendent before departure.

highlights.p: Stone blocks and aggregates from the Larvik district are among the hardest cargoes a hold can carry. Grab and loader impacts dent and abrade tank-top plating and lower hopper slopes, so a hold gauging after discharge is a sensible addition to the scope on ships in this trade.

The ferry to Hirtshals crosses the Skagerrak on a daily schedule. Engine-room pipework and selected car-deck areas can be measured while she lies in Larvik; tanks and shell plating wait for the docking, and we help the operator divide the scope sensibly.

highlights.h: A short way in from the sea
highlights.p: Larvik's quays are only a brief passage from the open Skagerrak, without the long fjord transit to Oslo or Drammen. Sea time to the berth is short, which helps when a lay day for gauging has to be added to a voyage at short notice.

port.h: Larvik, the Larviksfjord and a port shaped by stone and ferries
p: Larvik lies where the Numedalslågen river reaches the sea, at the head of the short Larviksfjord, west of the outer Oslofjord. The fairway from the open Skagerrak is brief compared with the long passage up to Oslo, and the fjord gives good shelter once a ship is inside. The town has a long maritime history: Colin Archer built his rescue boats here, along with the polar ship Fram, and generations of Larvik sailors and shipowners followed. Today the waterfront divides between the ferry terminal close to the town centre and the cargo port with its container, general cargo and bulk quays. Pilotage follows the national rules for the fjord approaches, and the port's limits on size keep most callers within the short-sea and smaller deep-sea classes rather than the largest bulk carriers.

The Hirtshals ferry is the most visible traffic: a large ro-pax ship carrying cars, coaches and freight trailers across the Skagerrak on a timetable that leaves it only a few hours alongside between crossings. The cargo port handles container feeders, general cargo ships and bulk ships. One trade is particular to the district. Larvikite, the blue-grey igneous stone that takes a high polish and is used in buildings worldwide, is quarried in the hills around Larvik, and stone has been shipped out through the port for generations. Aggregates and other bulk cargoes add further calls. Most of the ships are short-sea tonnage on European routes, with crews and managers who know the port and return to it regularly, which helps when a gauging scope is planned over more than one call.

Gauging windows in Larvik are short but predictable. The ferry keeps to its schedule and docks once a year, so engine-room and car-deck work is spread over turnarounds and tank work saved for the yard. Feeders and general cargo ships stay for the length of cargo operations, which is often less than a day. Bulk ships carrying stone or aggregates spend longer loading or discharging, and once a hold is clear its tank-top and lower plating can be reached. The fjord is sheltered and normally free of ice, so the main seasonal factor is the summer peak in ferry traffic, when the operator is least willing to release the ship for anything that might delay a sailing. Autumn and winter suit planned in-port work on the ferry better.

facilities.h: Where ships are measured in and around Larvik
p: The ferry berth, the container quay and the general cargo and bulk quays are the working locations. On the ferry, the chief engineer releases one system at a time during turnarounds and the team measures it while passengers and vehicles move above; car-deck work follows the vehicle flow and stops when loading starts. On cargo ships, measurement goes on alongside cargo work, with the team kept clear of crane and grab operations. Stone and aggregate cargoes leave dust and impact damage in the holds, so the tank-top usually needs sweeping before readings can be taken, and the ship is asked to plan for that as the hold empties.

Larvik is a cargo and ferry port rather than a docking port. The ferry and the cargo ships take their dockings at yards elsewhere on the Norwegian coast, in Denmark, in Poland or further afield, and readings from Larvik serve as a pre-docking estimate for those yards. Ships with a longer wait between cargoes can sometimes lie at a quay for a day or two, which is the best chance for ballast tank entry, since tanks can be emptied, ventilated and certified without competing with cargo handling.
list: Ferry terminal near the town centre — engine-room piping and car-deck plating on the Hirtshals ro-pax ship, released system by system during turnarounds.
Container quay — scrubber lines, deck plating and void spaces on feeders while containers are worked.
Bulk and general cargo quays — tank-top and hopper gauging on stone and aggregate carriers as each hold is cleared and swept.
Lay-by time at the cargo quays — ballast and double-bottom tanks on ships waiting between cargoes, once tanks are certified for entry.
Docking yards chosen by the owner — completion of renewal survey gauging after pre-docking readings taken in Larvik.

context.h: Port state control and cargo wear at Larvik
p: Foreign ships at Larvik are inspected by the Norwegian Maritime Authority under the Paris MoU. Short-sea general cargo and bulk ships calling here are often older tonnage, and port state control officers look closely at hatch covers, coamings, air pipes and ventilators, where wastage on these ships tends to show first. A detention, or a deficiency that class must clear before sailing, gives the owner little time, and readings taken at the berth can settle whether a temporary repair is enough to reach the next yard. Older short-sea ships trading to EU ports need an up-to-date Inventory of Hazardous Materials as well, which owners often renew at the docking where the steel work is done.

The wear that matters at Larvik comes from the cargo. Stone blocks are heavy and concentrated, and both blocks and crushed aggregates are loaded and discharged by grab, crane and front loader, which dents and abrades tank-top plating, scrapes hopper slopes and damages the lower parts of hold frames. Over years that mechanical wear combines with corrosion, especially where water collects at bilge wells and along the tank-top edges. Ferry car decks see a different load pattern, with heavy freight trailers on fixed lanes and lashing points loaded and released on every crossing, and fatigue cracking around supports and doublers is as much a concern there as thinning.

jobs.p: The jobs we see at Larvik are compact and planned around the call. For bulk and general cargo ships the request is often a hold condition check after a stone cargo, with readings on tank-tops, hoppers and lower frames; for the ferry it is pipework and car-deck plating over several turnarounds; for feeders it is scrubber pipework and deck plating during cargo work. Results go to the superintendent before the ship leaves, so a repair can be booked at the next suitable port or yard, and readings are laid out to match the ship's existing thickness measurement plan so they slot into the survey history. Common scopes include:
list: Tank-top, hopper and lower-frame gauging on a bulk ship after discharging stone blocks, with grab damage recorded alongside the thickness readings.
Engine-room sea-water and ballast piping on the Hirtshals ro-pax ship, measured over several turnarounds before its annual docking.
Car-deck plating, trailer-lane stiffeners and lashing-point doublers on the ferry, with magnetic particle testing at suspected fatigue cracks.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard lines on a container feeder, measured with the system off during cargo operations.
Hatch coaming and air-pipe readings on a short-sea general cargo ship following a port state control deficiency.

logistics: Sandefjord Airport Torp, a short drive from Larvik, has European and domestic flights, and Oslo Airport at Gardermoen is the alternative, with onward rail travel via Oslo on the Vestfold line. Passes for the ferry terminal and cargo quays are arranged by the ship's agent under ISPS, and the ferry operator adds its own safety briefing for work in passenger and vehicle areas. Larvik is in the Schengen area, so each technician from India needs a Schengen visa, and because ferry and feeder schedules are fixed, jobs here can usually be planned with a comfortable lead time.
vessels: Bulk carriers in the stone and aggregate trade

faqs.q: Can the Larvik–Hirtshals ferry be gauged in port?
faqs.a: Within limits. During turnarounds the chief engineer can release engine-room systems one at a time, and accessible car-deck areas can be measured while the deck is clear. Tanks, double bottoms and shell plating need emptying, entry permits or a dry hull, so they belong to the annual docking. We plan the in-port work over as many turnarounds as it takes, so that no crossing is delayed.

faqs.q: Why gauge holds after a stone cargo?
faqs.a: Stone blocks and aggregates strike the tank-top hard during loading and discharge, and grabs scrape hopper slopes and lower frames. That mechanical damage removes coating and some steel, and corrosion then speeds up in the scars. Gauging soon after discharge, with the damage recorded next to the readings, tells the owner whether the hold is still within allowable diminution or whether renewal should be planned before the next survey.

faqs.q: How much warning do you need for a Larvik job?
faqs.a: Enough to secure Schengen visas and flights for the team, which typically means several weeks unless the visas are already valid. Because ferry and feeder schedules are published well ahead, most Larvik work can be tied to a specific turnaround or call. For a ship on a one-off tramp call, send the expected dates as soon as the fixture is known.

faqs.q: Can ballast tanks be entered during a short cargo call at Larvik?
faqs.a: Only if the ship can empty, ventilate and certify the tanks for entry without disturbing cargo operations, which is difficult on a call of less than a day. When a ship has a lay day or waits between cargoes at the quay, ballast and double-bottom tanks become practical. Otherwise we concentrate the in-port scope on holds, decks and piping, and leave the tanks for a longer stop.
